fixture.note: 1.5 nm padding, not the notebook's 0.4: see the padding constraint.

cell_list.note: The host f64 and device f32 fractional bucketing agreed on all 5,002 atoms here. They are allowed to differ by one cell -- see the shape-aware criterion -- and did not.

neighbour_list_vs_cell_shell.note: Bit-identical forces, and the same trajectory over 49 rebuilds.

padding_constraint.rule: The 27-cell scan needs three cells an axis across the *perpendicular* widths. A rhombic dodecahedron's narrowest width is 0.707 of its edge, so it needs d >= 3*sqrt(2)*cutoff -- 4.24 nm at a 1 nm cutoff, against the cube's 3.0.
padding_constraint.consequence: 1L2Y at the notebook's 0.4 nm padding gives 2x2x2 cells and is refused; at 1.5 nm it gives 3x3x3 and runs. 5,002 atoms against the cube's 2,373 -- the volume saving per unit padding is real, but the minimum padding is larger, so a small solute can be better off in a cube.

rectangular_unchanged.note: The only movement across all six items was PME's, at the f32 ulp, recorded in engine-force-error-equilibrated-m3pro.json.
